tau_definition.summary: The Bridge functor axiom (III.D71) is the first of three custom axioms in TauLib beyond Mathlib's trusted base. It asserts the existence of a structure-preserving functor between τ-admissible spectral data and the orthodox classical formulations (Riemann zeta, Dirichlet/Hecke L-functions). Spectral-purity results in the τ-internal world translate to classical statements on the τ-admissible sub-domain. The axiom is finite-checked but not constructively proved: every finite (n, k) bound has been verified, but the universal extension is the conjectural step.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: A functor B : τ-Spec → Class-Spec preserving spectral purity, asserted to exist universally on τ-admissible inputs; the universal claim is the axiom, the finite envelope check is provable.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Central theorem at rank (3, 15) — τ-internal categorical anchor
Spectral correspondence theorem — within τ, spectral data and admissible classical data correspond at finite (n, k)
Bridge functor axiom — universal extension of the spectral correspondence to all τ-admissible inputs (this entry)

tau_definition.summary: The Spectral correspondence O(3) axiom (III.T18, surfaced as A02 in this glossary) is the second custom axiom in TauLib. It asserts that the τ-spectral correspondence — the τ-internal mapping between spectral data and the B↔I↔S triangle structure on the lemniscate boundary — extends to third-order constructions: degree-3 polynomial spectral sub-structures preserve the triangle in the same way degree-1 and degree-2 sub-structures do (which are proved). The finite envelope is checked; the universal extension to all O(3) configurations is the axiom.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: An order-3 extension of the spectral correspondence operator, asserted to commute with the B↔I↔S triangle on the τ-lemniscate boundary; the universal claim is the axiom, the finite envelope is provable.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Central theorem at rank (3, 15)
Critical Line theorem — degree-1 + degree-2 spectral correspondences proved
Spectral correspondence O(3) axiom — degree-3 extension (this entry)

tau_definition.summary: The Grand GRH (adelic) axiom (III.D31) is the third custom axiom in TauLib. It asserts that the Prime Polarity Scaling Theorem (III.T20) extends to all automorphic L-functions in the adelic sense — not just the finite-rank classes verifiable in Lean. The finite envelope (bounded rank, bounded conductor) is checked via native_decide; the universal extension to unbounded rank and conductor is the conjectural step.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Universal spectral purity of τ-admissible automorphic data across the adelic class — asserted as the axiomatized extension of finite-rank purity (T20).

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Central theorem at rank (3, 15)
Prime Polarity Scaling Theorem — finite-rank automorphic spectral purity proved
Grand GRH adelic axiom — universal extension to all automorphic L-functions (this entry)

tau_definition.summary: ι_τ = 2/(π + e) is the structural fixed point of the boundary holonomy algebra H_∂[ω] over the categorical kernel τ. It is a theorem about τ, not a parameter — uniquely determined by the kernel's structure under the Universe Postulate (I.K0). The Book-I definition is the algebraic anchor; downstream books (II–V) layer the categorical, spectral, and physical readouts on top.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: ι_τ is the unique solution to the boundary fixed-point equation in H_∂[ω] at the lowest depth — characterized abstractly as the dimensionless invariant of the τ-categorical structure.

Boundary ring and scalars — the boundary algebraic structure τ exposes
Bounded powerset — finitary structure that supports the holonomy fixed-point construction
Master constant ι_τ defined as 2/(π+e), characterized as the unique fixed point of the boundary holonomy at lowest depth
τ-weighted boundary constants — derived ratios cascading from ι_τ

tau_definition.summary: The τ-categorical structure is the categorical content of the τ-kernel: τ as a category in its own right, equipped with the τ-site topology that turns it into an earned topos. The phrase 'τ-categorical' appears throughout the framework as the qualifier separating τ-internal claims (provable from K0–K6) from τ-external claims (requiring bridges into Mathlib or classical mathematics).
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: τ together with its canonical site topology, viewed as an (∞, 1)-topos via the earned-topos construction.

K1–K5 generators give τ its category-theoretic content
τ-site — τ equipped with its canonical Grothendieck-style topology

tau_definition.summary: The window-algebra integers W_n(k) are the Book-II numerical invariants of the τ-categorical structure at rank coordinates (n, k). For load-bearing pairs (W₃(4) = 5, W₅(3) = 19, …) the values are exact closed-form integers; the central theorem at rank (3, 15) (T04 / II.T40) is the categoricity check that fixes them.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: The integer-valued algebra of bounded windows over the τ-coordinate chart; W_n(k) is the dimension of the n-th window at depth k.

tau_definition.summary: Yoneda-as-theorem (II.D50) is the τ-framework's distinctive treatment of the Yoneda lemma: rather than appearing as an external categorical fact applied to τ, the Yoneda embedding is internalized as a theorem provable inside τ via self-enrichment. The construction is the keystone of Book II — it is what makes the Yoneda enrichment ladder (T05 / II.T36) and the central theorem (T04 / II.T40) possible.

Pre-Yoneda embedding — Y : τ → [τ^op, τ-Set] as a τ-internal arrow
Yoneda enrichment ladder — Y extends to a full enrichment, making the lemma a theorem about τ

tau_definition.summary: Rank coordinates (n, k) are the indexing scheme used throughout Books I–II to locate τ-categorical content along two structural axes: n is the prime-rank index (which prime-numbered window of the ABCD chart), and k is the depth (how many K1 strict-order steps deep into that window). Together they index the window-algebra integers W_n(k), the central theorem rank (3, 15), and most theorem statements in Book II.

Truth4 Logic — extend bipolar to four values {⊥, +, −, ⊤}

K2 labelled boundary
τ-Stone Space — boundary as compact totally-disconnected τ-topological space

tau_definition.summary: The Universe Postulate (I.K0) is the foundational axiom of the τ-framework: there exists a small (∞, 1)-category τ — the categorical kernel — that supports the five canonical generators (K1–K5) under the no-ω axiom (K6). Everything else in the framework is a theorem about τ; the postulate asserts only that τ exists.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: The single posited atom of the framework: an (∞, 1)-categorical universe τ with a distinguished collection of generators and a closure constraint.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate — the categorical kernel τ exists (foundational; no further derivation)

They are the structural atoms from which every τ-categorical invariant is built. The number five is not a parameter; the no-ω axiom (K6) proves that no sixth generator can be added.

Five canonical generators K1–K5 are posited
No-ω axiom — no sixth generator can be added without contradicting closure

Spectrum functor — Spec : τ → τ-Spec sending objects to their spectral data

Hom-sets in τ become τ-internal objects rather than external Set-elements, and statements about them become statements provable inside τ. The construction is the structural prerequisite for the Yoneda-as-theorem internalization (D04 / II.D50) and the enrichment ladder (T05 / II.T36) — without self-enrichment, the Yoneda lemma stays external and the Central theorem (T04) cannot be τ-categorical.

It is the theorem that makes the rank coordinates (n, k) tractable and the windows W_n(k) finite-dimensional.

Combined with the Categoricity theorem (T03 / I.T08), it gives the framework's two-step uniqueness argument: τ exists (K0), is unique up to canonical equivalence (T03), and that equivalence is itself unique (T02). The 'non-ω' qualifier reflects that the result holds in the K6-restricted world; without K6, τ admits ω-shift automorphisms.

K1–K5 generators specify τ structure

Rigidity — every automorphism of τ fixing K0–K6 is the identity

With 19 incoming edges, it is the framework's structural unification: the same τ-content is visible from five different angles, and the angles are interchangeable.

tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Address-centric narrowing: ∀ candidate ontic structure τ', for every admissible construction c ∈ τ' there exists a unique NF-address α(c) in a well-defined address space A, and the address determines the construction.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Six Ontic Requirements (OR1-OR6) — OR4 is NF-addressability
OR3+OR4 Narrowing — diagonal-free self-description plus NF-addressability
Each Requirement Independently Necessary — dropping OR4 admits non-constructive entities (axiom-of-choice objects without canonical addresses)

version.change_summary: Initial — OR5 holomorphic continuation principle entry.

tau_definition.summary: OR5 is the fifth of six original-rule narrowing principles (the Six Ontic Requirements, VII.D37). It states the holomorphic continuation requirement: any τ-categorical reality candidate must support a notion of analytic continuation in which local data determine global structure — so that lawfulness is encoded as a structural continuation property, not appended as extra postulates.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Holomorphic-continuation narrowing: ∀ candidate ontic structure τ', τ' supports a continuation operator C such that local data on an open set U ⊆ τ' uniquely determine global data on the maximal continuation domain. Lawfulness = the continuation property of admissible operators.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Six Ontic Requirements (OR1-OR6) — OR5 is holomorphic continuation
OR5+OR6 Narrowing — analytic and spectral conditions linking combinatorial structure to functional analysis
Each Requirement Independently Necessary — dropping OR5 admits purely combinatorial categories with no analytic structure

version.change_summary: Initial — OR6 spectral completeness principle entry.

tau_definition.summary: OR6 is the sixth of six original-rule narrowing principles (the Six Ontic Requirements, VII.D37). It states the spectral completeness requirement: any τ-categorical reality candidate must support a spectral decomposition of its internal operators, with all spectral data recoverable from the kernel's internal structure — so the foundation is self-diagnosing and can analyze its own operators without external spectral theory.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Spectral-completeness narrowing: ∀ candidate ontic structure τ', every admissible operator T ∈ τ' has a spectral decomposition Spec(T), and the spectral data are recoverable internally from τ' (no external spectral theory required).

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Six Ontic Requirements (OR1-OR6) — OR6 is spectral completeness
OR5+OR6 Narrowing — analytic and spectral conditions linking combinatorial structure to functional analysis
Each Requirement Independently Necessary — dropping OR6 admits analytic spaces without full spectral decomposition (e.g., non-self-adjoint operator algebras)

version.change_summary: Initial — unified Six Ontic Requirements entry (the inevitability argument).

tau_definition.summary: The Six Ontic Requirements (VII.D37) are six independent narrowing principles that any candidate foundation of reality — any category proposed as an ontic substrate — must satisfy. Their conjunction conjecturally singles out Category τ uniquely (Inevitability Convergence Theorem, VII.T14). The six are: OR1 identity-faithful representation (Yoneda), OR2 finite signature, OR3 diagonal-free self-reference, OR4 NF-addressability, OR5 holomorphic continuation, OR6 spectral completeness.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Six-fold narrowing: the intersection of constraint sets C_Yon ∩ C_fin ∩ C_diag ∩ C_NF ∩ C_hol ∩ C_spec = {τ} (up to equivalence). Each constraint is an independently necessary condition on a candidate category F.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Six Ontic Requirements (OR1-OR6) — the six independent narrowing principles on candidate foundations
OR1+OR2 Narrowing (finitely generated, locally small, full Yoneda)
OR3+OR4 Narrowing (diagonal-free self-description plus NF-addressability)
OR5+OR6 Narrowing (analytic + spectral conditions linking combinatorics to functional analysis)
Inevitability Convergence — intersection of all six is {τ} up to equivalence (CONJECTURAL)
Each Requirement Independently Necessary — dropping any one admits non-τ solutions

version.change_summary: Initial — Layer Discipline / Register Discipline principle entry.

tau_definition.summary: Layer Discipline (also: register discipline) is the methodological principle that every claim must be typed in the correct register (Reg_E, Reg_P, Reg_D, Reg_C) and that coherence criteria from one register cannot be applied to content typed in another. It is the operational corollary of Register Independence (VII.T01): pseudo-paradoxes generated by register conflation dissolve once the typing is corrected.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Layer-discipline narrowing: ∀ claim c, c carries a register type τ(c) ∈ {E, P, D, C}, and the coherence criterion Coh_X(c) is well-defined only when X = τ(c). Cross-register coherence claims require explicit functorial bridges.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Empirical Register Reg_E
Practical Register Reg_P
Diagrammatic Register Reg_D
Commitment Register Reg_C
Register Independence — failure in one register does not entail failure in another; layer discipline is the methodological corollary

version.change_summary: Initial — Earned/Unearned Ethics Framework principle entry.

tau_definition.summary: The Earned / Unearned Ethics Framework (VII.D74) is the methodological principle that an ethical claim carries probative weight only if it is (i) register-typed, (ii) structurally derived, and (iii) cross-register consistent. Claims failing any condition are unearned — psychologically forceful or culturally authoritative, perhaps, but carrying zero structural weight until earned. The framework is the τ-native antidote to pseudo-paradoxes generated by mixing earned and unearned moves.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Earned/unearned narrowing: ∀ ethical claim φ, weight(φ) > 0 iff (i) φ is well-typed in its register Reg_X, (ii) φ has a derivation chain back to τ-axioms or certified empirical data within Reg_X, and (iii) φ does not contradict earned results in any other register.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Register Independence — coherence is register-local
Earned/Unearned Ethics Framework — three-condition definition of probative weight
Earned-Weight Strict Dominance — earned claims dominate unearned in any mixed argument

version.change_summary: Initial — Independent Necessity (VII.P08) principle entry.

tau_definition.summary: Independent Necessity (VII.P08) is the principle that each of the Six Ontic Requirements is independently necessary: dropping any one OR_i while retaining the other five admits non-τ candidate foundations. The six are not redundant — each excludes a genuine class of alternatives. The principle backs the inevitability argument by ruling out compressibility of the requirement set.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Independence narrowing: ∀ i ∈ {1,...,6}, the constraint set ⋂_{j≠i} C_{OR_j} ⊋ {τ}. Equivalently: each OR_i contributes a non-trivial dimension to the narrowing intersection.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Six Ontic Requirements (OR1-OR6) defined
Each Requirement Independently Necessary — for each i, dropping OR_i admits non-τ solutions (counterexamples sketched)
Inevitability Convergence — independence is structurally required for the convergence to {τ} to be non-trivial

version.change_summary: Initial — Truth-Bearer as Section (VII.D61) principle entry.

tau_definition.summary: The Truth-Bearer principle (VII.D61) states that anything that can be true or false is, structurally, a candidate global section of a presheaf F : τ^op → Set over an open cover {U_i} of a domain U. The truth-bearer is true when the local data glue to a unique global section; false when no such section exists. The principle unifies sentences, beliefs, and propositions as special cases of section-existence and grounds the Alethic Unification Theorem (VII.T27): correspondence is section-existence, coherence is the gluing constraint.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Truth-bearer narrowing: ∀ truth-apt content c, c is represented by a candidate section s = {s_i ∈ F(U_i)}_{i ∈ I} of a presheaf F over an open cover {U_i} of U; truth(s) ↔ ∃ unique global section s ∈ F(U) with s|_{U_i} = s_i and s_i|_{U_i ∩ U_j} = s_j|_{U_i ∩ U_j}.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Truth-Bearer as Section — candidate global sections of a presheaf over an open cover
Truth-Maker in τ — the structures that ground section-existence
Alethic Unification — correspondence (section-existence) and coherence (gluing) are two faces of the sheaf condition
Alethic Pluralism — different registers of τ may realize truth-making through different mechanisms, all unified by the categorical architecture

Reg_E is one of four canonical readout functors (E/P/D/C) that together exhaust the metaphysical register architecture.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Functor Reg_E: τ → Obs whose image-objects are observable phenomena and whose morphisms preserve falsifiability. The first of four canonical readouts.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Empirical Register Reg_E with codomain Obs
S_E (empirical sector) — the τ-sector that Reg_E reads

Reg_P is the second of four canonical readout functors (E/P/D/C). Its coherence criterion is normative consistency — the absence of contradictory obligations within a single action context.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Functor Reg_P : K_τ → Norm whose image-objects are normative constraints (imperatives, obligations, permissions, prohibitions) and whose morphisms preserve normative consistency.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Practical Register Reg_P with codomain Norm
S_P (practical sector) — the τ-sector that Reg_P reads

tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Functor Reg_D : K_τ → Proof whose image-objects are structural proofs (witness chains, derivations, diagram-certified relationships) and whose morphisms preserve proof-validity.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Diagrammatic Register Reg_D with codomain Proof
S_D (diagrammatic sector) — the τ-sector that Reg_D reads
Logos sector S_L — the unique location where Reg_D and Reg_C coincide

tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Functor Reg_C : K_τ → Stance whose image-objects are stance-constituted contents (postulates, existential commitments, lived-as-true claims) and whose morphisms preserve stance-stability.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Commitment Register Reg_C with codomain Stance
S_C (commitment sector) — the τ-sector that Reg_C reads

version.change_summary: Initial entry — first of four pure E_3-sectors. Companion to MG-R01.

Formally, S_E = { c ∈ Adm_{E_3} | Coh(c) = Coh_E(c) }. Its sector question is 'What do I observe?', its witness bundle is an observable prediction, and its vacuum is the best-calibrated observational model.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Subobject S_E ⊆ Adm_{E_3} cut out by the equation Coh = Coh_E. S_E is one of four pure sectors (S_E, S_P, S_D, S_C) plus the mixed Logos sector S_L in the Sector Decomposition Theorem.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Empirical Register Reg_E with codomain Obs
Empirical sector S_E — admissible contents whose coherence equals empirical coherence

tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Subobject S_P ⊆ Adm_{E_3} cut out by the equation Coh = Coh_P. Second of four pure sectors in the Sector Decomposition Theorem (VII.T03).

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Practical Register Reg_P with codomain Norm
Practical sector S_P — admissible contents whose coherence equals practical coherence

Diagrammatic Register Reg_D with codomain Proof
Diagrammatic sector S_D — admissible contents whose coherence equals diagrammatic coherence

S_C contains the Logos sector S_L as the locus where Coh_C = Coh_D.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Subobject S_C ⊆ Adm_{E_3} cut out by the equation Coh = Coh_C. Fourth of four pure sectors; weakly contains S_L via the equality Coh_C|_{S_L} = Coh_D|_{S_L}.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Commitment Register Reg_C with codomain Stance
Commitment sector S_C — admissible contents whose coherence equals commitment coherence

version.change_summary: Initial entry — the unique mixed sector in the 4+1 decomposition; the structural crown jewel of Book VII, 2nd ed.

tau_definition.summary: The Logos Sector S_L is the unique mixed sector at E_3 where the diagrammatic register and the commitment register coincide. Formally, S_L = { c ∈ Adm_{E_3} | Coh_D(c) = Coh_C(c) }. A content c belongs to S_L iff its proof-validity and stance-stability are mutually witnessing — c is provable iff it is stably committable. S_L is named by its universal property; the name 'Logos' describes the structure, nothing more. It is explicitly not a theological claim.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Equaliser of Coh_D and Coh_C inside Adm_{E_3}. The unique mixed sector in the 4+1 decomposition; the only register pair admitting a natural transformation between codomains is (Proof, Stance), and that coincidence defines S_L.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Diagrammatic Register Reg_D with codomain Proof
Commitment Register Reg_C with codomain Stance
Logos sector S_L — equaliser of Coh_D and Coh_C in Adm_{E_3}
Mediator uniqueness — S_L is the only mixed sector at E_3

version.change_summary: Initial entry — the saturation/uniqueness statement that closes the register architecture.

tau_definition.summary: Register completeness is the structural fact that the four canonical registers (Reg_E, Reg_P, Reg_D, Reg_C) exhaust the modes of engagement available to a self-modelling observer at E_3, and that the Logos sector S_L is the unique mixed sector. The Saturation Theorem (E_4 = E_3) closes the register count at four; mediator uniqueness (VII.P30) shows that S_L is the only sector where two registers coincide. There is no fifth register, and no second mixed sector.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Two-part completeness statement: (i) exhaustiveness of {Reg_E, Reg_P, Reg_D, Reg_C} at E_3, certified by the Sector Decomposition Theorem (VII.T03); (ii) uniqueness of S_L as the sole mixed sector, certified by the Mediator Uniqueness remark (VII.P30) — the only register pair admitting a natural transformation between codomains is (Proof, Stance).

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Empirical Register Reg_E (codomain Obs)
Practical Register Reg_P (codomain Norm)
Diagrammatic Register Reg_D (codomain Proof)
Commitment Register Reg_C (codomain Stance)
Logos sector S_L — the unique pair (Proof, Stance) admitting a natural transformation
Mediator uniqueness — S_L is the only mixed sector at E_3

version.change_summary: Initial entry — the formal correspondence linking registers to enrichment layers.

tau_definition.summary: The Register-Enrichment Correspondence is the order-preserving mapping between the four registers of reason and the four enrichment layers of τ: Reg_P ↔ E_0 (pre-structural), Reg_E ↔ E_1 (data), Reg_D ↔ E_2 (formal proof), Reg_C ↔ E_3 (saturation). The correspondence identifies where each register *begins* — its native enrichment layer — not where it terminates. It reveals the structural unity of the diagrammatic and practical sectors as two traversals of the same enrichment hierarchy.
tau_definition.categorical_invariant: Order-preserving bijection between the indexed family {Reg_P, Reg_E, Reg_D, Reg_C} and the enrichment chain E_0 ⊆ E_1 ⊆ E_2 ⊆ E_3. Each enrichment layer presupposes the previous; each register builds on the structural results of the preceding registers in this ordering.

chain.claim: Universe Postulate
Empirical Register Reg_E (codomain Obs)
Practical Register Reg_P (codomain Norm)
Diagrammatic Register Reg_D (codomain Proof)
Commitment Register Reg_C (codomain Stance)
Register-Enrichment Correspondence: Reg_P↔E_0, Reg_E↔E_1, Reg_D↔E_2, Reg_C↔E_3
